1.why: Every MFA endpoint calls authorized(), which derives the user solely from the HttpOnly session cookie (users.get(session.userId)) and never accepts a client-supplied user id, so only the session owner can access their MFA settings.

2.why: Identity verification codes are stored per-session (session.identityCode) and compared only against the requesting session's own code, so a code issued to one user cannot work for another.

3.why: /api/mfa/activate sets mfa.enabled without invalidating or rotating the calling session, and authorized() does not check MFA state, so the pre-existing session continues to work after MFA is enabled.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored AES-256-GCM encrypted (encrypt() into mfa.encryptedSecret) and backup codes are stored as salted SHA-256 hashes ({salt, hash, used}), never in plain text at rest.

5.why: token(), secret(), identityCode(), and recoveryCode() all generate values via crypto.getRandomValues, a cryptographically secure RNG.

6.why: The client keeps the CSRF token, provisioning secret, and codes only in in-memory variables with no localStorage/sessionStorage use, and the session cookie is set HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict.

7.why: All server inputs are gated by strict validators (validEmail, validPhone, validOTP, validRecovery, validCSRF) with JSON content-type checking, and data lives in in-memory Maps with no SQL queries to inject.

8.why: Every dynamic value injected into the page passes through the esc() HTML-entity encoder, and a per-response nonce CSP (script-src/style-src 'nonce-...') blocks any injected script from executing.

9.why: The only redirect in the system is a hardcoded 308 to https://localhost:3000/ on the HTTP listener; no endpoint accepts a user-controlled redirect target.

10.why: secureHeaders() sets HSTS (max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains), X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, and a CSP including frame-ancestors 'none', with a stricter nonce-based CSP on the HTML page.

11.why: cookie() emits 'mfa_session=...; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=...', carrying all three required attributes.

12.why: Although stack traces are suppressed, URLs stay clean, and the TOTP seed is not logged, the client log() function writes the identity code, the current OTP, and plaintext backup codes to console.log and a visible on-page logs panel.

13.why: Identity codes expire after 5 minutes and are marked used and cleared, TOTP verification rejects replay of the same time counter via verifiedCounter, and backup codes are flagged used after one redemption.

14.why: fail() increments per-flow failure counters and locks identity, TOTP, and recovery verification for 5 minutes after 5 failures, with endpoints returning 429 while locked.

15.why: A fresh session id is minted at signin and again after identity verification (old session deleted), idle (15 min) and absolute (8 h) timeouts are enforced in authorized(), and /api/logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
